name: City Council Meeting - Sep 10, 2024
agenda_text:
TORRANCE CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
  SEPTEMBER 10, 2024
  ADJOURNED REGULAR MEETING
  5:00 P.M. - CLOSED SESSION
  6:30 P.M. - REGULAR BUSINESS BEGINS
  IN COUNCIL CHAMBER AT 3031 TORRANCE BL.

Revised City Council Agenda 9-10-24

* Denotes the item was added after posting of the agenda.

OPENING CEREMONIES

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  ROLL CALL
  : Councilmembers Gerson, Kaji, Kalani, Lewis, Mattucci, Sheikh, and Mayor Chen

14.  CLOSED SESSION

  14A. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR (California Government Code
  §54957.6): Agency Negotiator: Aram Chaparyan Employee
  Organization/Association:
  1. Certain Full-Time Salaried and Hourly Employees
  2. Certain Part-Time Hourly Employees
  3. Crossing Guards
  4. Elected Officials
  5. Engineers and Torrance Fiscal Employees Association
  6. Executive & Management Employees
  7. Police & Fire Trainees
  8. Safety Management Employees
  9. Torrance City Employees Association
  10. Fire Safety Management
  11. Torrance Fire Fighters Association
  12. Torrance Library Employees Association
  13. Torrance Municipal Employees/AFSCME Local 1117 AFL-CIO
  14. Torrance Police Commanders Association (TPCA)
  15. Torrance Police Officers Association
  16. Torrance Professional Parks & Recreation Employees Organization
  17. Torrance Professional & Supervisory Association
  18. Torrance Recurrent Recreational Employees Organization
  19. City Treasurer
  20. City Attorney
  21. City Manager
  14A - STAFF REPORT

  14B. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION (Significant
  Exposure to Litigation Pursuant to California Government Code § 54956.9(d)(2)):
  One case

  14C. REAL PROPERTY – CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR
  (California Government Code §54956.8):
  1)  Property: 18301 Kingsdale Avenue, Redondo Beach, CA 90278 Agency Negotiator:
  Aram Chaparyan Negotiating Parties: City of Torrance and Torrance Unified School
  District Under Negotiation: Price, terms and conditions of Park Redevelopment
  Proposal

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

10A. City Manager – Conduct Closed Hearing on the Appeal of the Civil Service
   Commission Decision Sustaining the Termination of a Police Officer (8). Confidential
  under Penal Code 832.7 and Copley Press v. Superior Court 39 Cal. 4th 1272 (2006).
  Consideration of Public Employee Discipline will be Conducted in Closed Session per
  California Government Code Section 54957(b)(1), Unless the Employee Requests to
  Have the Appeal Conducted in Public Session. The Deliberation of This Matter by the
  City Council will Occur in Closed Session. Expenditure: None.
  10A - STAFF REPORT

RECONVENE

2.  FLAG SALUTE: Councilmember Mattucci NON-SECTARIAN INVOCATION:
  Councilmember Sheikh

3.  REPORT OF THE CITY CLERK ON THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA The agenda was
  posted on the Public Notice Board at 3031 Torrance Bl. and on the City’s Website on
  Wednesday, September 04, 2024 /s/ Rebecca Poirier
  3 - AFFIDAVIT
  3 - REVISED AFFIDAVIT

MOTION TO WAIVE FURTHER READING OF RESOLUTIONS AND ORDINANCES AFTER
NUMBER & TITLE – See Council Rules of Order Section 2.11 (Resolution 2006-65)

4.  ANNOUNCEMENT OF WITHDRAWN, DEFERRED, AND/OR SUPPLEMENTAL ITEMS

5.  COUNCIL COMMITTEE MEETINGS AND ANNOUNCEMENTS

6.  COMMUNITY MATTERS

  6A. RESOLUTION NO. 2024-63 honoring Gilbert Ortega upon his retirement from the
  City of Torrance after thirty-six years of service. (For Adoption Only)
  6A - STAFF REPORT

  6B. City Manager – Appoint Torrance Representative to South Bay Workforce
  Investment Board. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council appoint Catherine Holdbrook-Smith
  as representative to the South Bay Workforce Investment Board for the City of Torrance.
  6B - STAFF REPORT

* The following item was added on Saturday, September 7, 2024.

  6C. Recognition of Torrance Babe Ruth Baseball Teams

7.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS #1 (Limited up to a 15-minute period) This portion of the
  meeting is reserved for comments on items under the Consent Calendar or items that
  are not on the agenda. Under the Ralph M. Brown Act, City Council cannot act on
  items raised during public comment, but may respond briefly to statements made or
  questions posed; request clarification; or refer the item to staff. Speakers under Orals
  are limited to either Oral Communications #1 or Oral Communications #2 and no
  longer than 1 minute per speaker. Time starts when you step up to the microphone. If
  presenting handout material to Council, please provide 11 copies to the City Clerk
  before speaking. Handouts will be distributed while you speak.
  PUBLIC COMMENT
  PUBLIC COMMENT RECEIVED AFTER 5:30 P.M. ON 9/9/24 AND BEFORE 10:41 P.M. ON
  9/10/2024

8.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  Matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion and one
  vote. There will be no separate discussion of these items. If discussion is desired, that item will be removed by
  a Councilmember from the Consent Calendar and considered separately..

  8A. City Clerk – Approve City Council Minutes. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Clerk that City Council approve the City Council minutes of
  August 13, 2024 and August 20, 2024.
 8B. Community Services – Authorize Library Commission to Conduct Six (6)
  Regularly Scheduled Meetings at Various Branch Libraries from December 2024
  through June 2025. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Community Services Director that City Council authorize the
  Library Commission to conduct six (6) regularly scheduled meetings at various branch
  libraries from December 2024 through June 2025.
  8B - STAFF REPORT

8C. City Manager – Authorize Recognition and Attornment Agreement for Subtenant
  of City-Owned Property Known as Rolling Hills Plaza (C-053). Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council authorize a Recognition and
  Attornment Agreement by and among Rolling Hills Plaza, LLC, a California limited liability
  company, Veterinary Emergency Group, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, and the
  City of Torrance with regard to a sublease of City-owned property located at the corner of
  Pacific Coast Highway and Crenshaw Boulevard, also known as Rolling Hills Plaza (C-053).
  8C - STAFF REPORT

8D. Community Development – Approve Final Parcel Map No. 83385, Accept City
  Street and Highway Easement, and Determine that the Project is Categorically
  Exempt by the 2021 Guidelines for Implementation of the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), Article 19, Sections 15303 and 15315.
  Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Community Development Director that City Council:
  1) Approve Final Parcel Map No. 83385; and
  2) Accept an easement of variable width along Crenshaw Boulevard for public street and
  highway purposes; and
  3) Determine that the project is categorically exempt by the 2021 Guidelines for
  Implementation of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), Article 19, Sections
  15303 and 15315.
  8D - STAFF REPORT

8E.  Community Services – Approve First Amendment to Contract Services
  Agreement for Encampment Prevention Overnight Security Guard Services.
  Expenditure: Not-to-Exceed $220,000 (Non-General Fund).
  Recommendation of the Community Services Director that City Council approve a first
  amendment to the contract services agreement with Absolute International Security, Inc. of
  Irwindale, CA (C2023-124) in the amount of $220,000, for a new not-to-exceed amount of
  $419,912.32, to provide encampment prevention overnight security guard services at
  various city parks and facilities and extend the term for a one-year period beginning
  September 12, 2024 and ending September 11, 2025.
  8E - STAFF REPORT

8F.  Community Services – Accept and File 2023 Torrance Sister City Association
  (TSCA) Annual Report and Financial Statement. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Community Services Director that City Council accept and file the
  2023 Torrance Sister City Association (TSCA) Annual Report and Financial Statement.
  8F - STAFF REPORT

8G. Torrance Youth Council and Community Services – Accept and File Torrance
  Youth Council 2023-24 Annual Report. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Torrance Youth Council and Community Services Director that City
  Council accept and file the Torrance Youth Council 2023-24 Annual Report.
  8G - STAFF REPORT

8H. Parks and Recreation Commission and Community Services – Accept and File
  2023-24 Parks and Recreation Commission Annual Report. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Parks and Recreation Commission and Community Services
  Director that City Council accept and file the 2023-24 Parks and Recreation Commission
  Annual Report.
  8H - STAFF REPORT

8I.  Cultural Arts Commission and Community Services – Accept and File 2023-24
   Cultural Arts Commission Annual Report. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Cultural Arts Commission and Community Services Director that
  City Council accept and file the 2023-24 Cultural Arts Commission Annual Report.
  8I - STAFF REPORT

  8J.  Library Commission and Community Services – Accept and File 2023-24 Library
  Commission Annual Report. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Library Commission and Community Services Director that City
  Council accept and file the 2023-24 Library Commission Annual Report.
  8J - STAFF REPORT

  8K. Commission on Aging and Community Services – Accept and File 2023-24
  Commission on Aging Annual Report. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Commission on Aging and Community Services Director that City
  Council accept and file the 2023-24 Commission on Aging Annual Report.
  8K - STAFF REPORT

  8L.  Measure SST Citizens’ Oversight Committee and Finance – Accept and File 2023-
  24 Measure SST Citizens’ Oversight Committee Annual Report. Expenditure:
  None.
  Recommendation of the Measure SST Citizens’ Oversight Committee and Finance Director
  that City Council accept and file the 2023-24 Measure SST Citizens’ Oversight Committee
  Annual Report.
  8L - STAFF REPORT

  8M. City Manager – Approve First Amendment to Consulting Services Agreement for
  Torrance Civic Center Master Plan and Economic Study. Expenditure: $18,108.20
  (General Fund).
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council approve a first amendment to the
  consulting services agreement with Gruen Associates of Los Angeles, CA (C2023-105)
  authorizing a 10% contingency in the amount of $18,108.20, for a new not-to-exceed
  amount of $199,190.20, to cover future unforeseen costs, and to extend the contract term
  for an additional year beginning July 31, 2024 and ending July 31, 2025.
  8M - STAFF REPORT

  8N. General Services – Accept and File Update on Use of Unleaded Aviation Gas at
  Torrance Municipal Airport – Zamperini Field. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the General Services Director that City Council accept and file an
  update on the use of unleaded aviation gas at Torrance Municipal Airport - Zamperini Field.
  8N - STAFF REPORT
  8N - SUPPLEMENTAL

9.  ADMINISTRATIVE MATTERS

  9A. City Manager and Community Services – Adopt RESOLUTION Approving a Deed
  Restriction for City-owned Property Located at the Northeast Corner of Madrona
  Avenue and Sepulveda Boulevard, Commonly Known as Madrona Marsh
  Preserve. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager and Community Services Director that City Council
  adopt a RESOLUTION approving a Deed Restriction to and for the benefit of California
  Department of Parks and Recreation for a 2002 Resources Bond Act, Outdoor
  Environmental Education Facilities Grant Program Award on City-owned property located at
  the northeast corner of Madrona Avenue and Sepulveda Boulevard, commonly known as
  Madrona Marsh Preserve (APN: 7359-002-901, 7359-002-903, and 7359-002-904).
  9A - STAFF REPORT

  9B. Community Services – Discuss and Provide Direction on Torrance Sister City
  2024 Grant Application Request. Expenditure: $5,000 (General Fund).
  Recommendation of the Community Services Director that City Council discuss and provide
  direction on the Torrance Sister City Association’s 2024 grant application request in the
  amount of $5,000, pending City Council approval.
  9B - STAFF REPORT
 9C. Armed Forces Day Special Standing Committee – Accept and File June 24, 2024
  Meeting Minutes and Discuss and Provide Direction on 2025 Armed Forces Day
  Parade and Celebration. Expenditures: None.
  Recommendation of the Armed Forces Day Special Standing Committee that City Council:
  1) Accept and file the June 24, 2024 Armed Forces Day Special Standing Committee
  meeting minutes; and
  2) Discuss and provide direction on the program and events for the 2025 Armed Forces
  Day Parade and Celebration.
  9C - STAFF REPORT

9D. City Council Strategic Plan Committee – Accept and File City Council Strategic
  Plan Implementation Program Update and Meeting Minutes. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Council Strategic Plan Committee that City Council:
  1) Accept and file June 12, 2024 Council Strategic Plan Committee meeting minutes; and
  2) Accept and file June 12, 2024 Council Strategic Plan Committee Implementation
  Program Update.
  9D - STAFF REPORT

9E.  City Manager – Adopt RESOLUTION Setting Forth Hours, Wages, and Working
  Conditions for Police Safety Management Employees. Expenditure: $283,304
  (General Fund: Approximately $141,652 Annually).
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council:
  1) Adopt a RESOLUTION setting forth the hours, wages, and working conditions for
  Police Safety Management employees; and
  2) Repeal Resolution No. 2019-82 in its entirety.
  9E - STAFF REPORT

9F.  City Manager – Adopt RESOLUTION Setting Forth Hours, Wages, and Working
  Conditions for Executive and Management Employees. Expenditure: $4,712,077
  (General Fund and Non-General Fund: Approximately $1,178,019 Annually).
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council:
  1) Adopt a RESOLUTION setting forth the hours, wages, and working conditions for
  Executive and Management employees; and
  2) Approve employee general increase rate of 4% for FY2024-25, 4% for FY2025-26, 4%
  for FY2026-27, and 4% for FY2027-28; and
  3) Approve merit pool funding for FY2024-25, FY2025-26, FY2026-27, and FY2027-28;
  and
  4) Repeal Resolution No. 2024-18 in its entirety.
  9F - STAFF REPORT

9G. City Manager – Adopt RESOLUTIONS Setting Forth Hours, Wages, and Working
  Conditions for Fire Safety Management Employees and Torrance Fire Chief
  Officers Association. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council:
  1) Adopt a RESOLUTION amending Torrance Fire Chief Officers Association Resolution
  2014-03 and Fire Safety Management Resolutions 2017-30, 2018-63, and 2019-84
  setting forth the hours, wages, and working conditions for Fire Safety Management
  employees; and
  2) Adopt a RESOLUTION setting forth the hours, wages, and working conditions for Fire
  Safety Management employees; and
  3) Repeal Resolution No. 2024-14 in its entirety.
  9G - STAFF REPORT

9H. City Manager – Adopt RESOLUTION Setting Forth Hours, Wages, and Working
  Conditions for Certain Full-Time Salaried and Hourly Employees. Expenditure:
  $1,600,429 (General Fund and Non-General Fund: Approximately $400,107
  Annually).
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council:
  1) Adopt a RESOLUTION setting forth the hours, wages, and working conditions for
  Certain Full-Time Salaried and Hourly employees ; and
  2) Repeal Resolution No. 2022-144 in its entirety.
  9H - STAFF REPORT

9I.  City Manager – Adopt RESOLUTION Pursuant to Memorandum of Understanding
   (MOU) Setting Forth Hours, Wages, and Working Conditions for Torrance
  Professional & Supervisory Association (TPSA). Expenditure: $3,346,000
  (General Fund and Non-General Fund: Approximately $836,500 Annually).
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council adopt a RESOLUTION pursuant to
  memorandum of understanding (MOU) setting forth the hours, wages, and working
  conditions for employees represented by the Torrance Professional & Supervisory
  Association (TPSA) for the period beginning July 1, 2024, and ending June 30, 2028.
  9I - STAFF REPORT PART 1
  9I - STAFF REPORT PART 2
  9I - SUPPLEMENTAL

9J.  City Manager – Adopt RESOLUTIONS Amending Benefits Section for City
  Attorney, City Manager, City Treasurer; and Compensation and Insurance for
  Elected Officials. Expenditure: $36,822 (General Fund).
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council:
  1) Adopt a RESOLUTION amending Resolution No. 2024-34 setting forth changes
  regarding hours, wages, and working conditions for the City Attorney in the amount of
  $2,393 which updates the City Contribution for Employee Health Insurance; and
  2) Adopt a RESOLUTION amending Resolution No 2020-97 setting forth changes
  regarding hours, wages, and working conditions for the City Manager, which updates
  the City Contribution for Employee Health Insurance; and
  3) Adopt a RESOLUTION amending Resolution No. 2018-110 setting forth changes
  regarding hours, wages, and working conditions for the City Treasurer in the amount of
  $2,393 which updates the City Contribution for Employee Health Insurance; and
  4) Adopt a RESOLUTION amending Resolution No 2023-29 setting forth changes
  regarding hours, wages, and working conditions for Elected Officials, in the amount of
  $32,036 which updates the City Contribution for Employee Health Insurance and
  increases the City Clerk’s pay rate by 9%.
  9J - STAFF REPORT

9K. City Manager – Approve Side Letter Agreements Regarding Implementation of
  Torrance Police Department Enhanced Recruitment and Retention Incentive Pilot
  Program. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council:
  1) Approve a side letter agreement between the Torrance City Employees Association
  (TCEA) and Management to implement Enhanced Recruitment and Retention Pilot
  Program; and
  2) Approve a side letter agreement between the Torrance Municipal Employees -
  AFSCME Local 1117 (TME-AFSCME) and Management to implement Enhanced
  Recruitment and Retention Pilot Program; and
  3) Approve a side letter agreement between the Torrance Police Commanders
  Association (TPCA) and Management to implement Enhanced Recruitment and
  Retention Pilot Program; and
  4) Approve a side letter agreement between the Torrance Professional and Supervisory
  Association (TPSA) and Management to implement Enhanced Recruitment and
  Retention Pilot Program.
  9K - STAFF REPORT
  9K - SUPPLEMENTAL
  9K - MATERIALS AVAILABLE

9L.  Citizen Development and Enrichment Committee – Discuss and Provide
  Direction on Appropriated Resource Contributions for the Neighborhood
  Coordinated Seaside Ranchos Holiday Lights Display, Discuss and Consider
  Adopting an ORDINANCE Amending the Torrance Municipal Code Pertaining to
  “Cottage Food”, and Accept and File Meeting Minutes. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Citizen Development and Enrichment Committee that City Council:
  1) Discuss and provide direction on the appropriated resource contributions to the
  neighborhood coordinated Seaside Ranchos Holiday Lights Display; and
  2) Discuss and consider amending the Cottage Food Ordinance; and
  3) Adopt an ORDINANCE amending Torrance Municipal Code (TMC) Section
  415.1.040(b) “Operating Standards” and Repealing Section 415.1.050 “Pilot Program”
  of Division 4 “Public Health and Welfare”, Chapter 15 “Cottage Food”; and
  4) Approve an Ordinance Summary for publication; and
  5) Accept and file the Citizen Development and Enrichment Committee meeting minutes
   from May 15, 2024.
  9L - STAFF REPORT
  9L- MATERIALS AVAILABLE

RECESS

RECONVENE

10.  HEARINGS

  10B. Finance – Conduct Public Hearing, Adopt RESOLUTION Adopting a Statement of
  Goals and Policies for the Use of the Mello-Roos Community Facilities Act of
  1982, Adopt ORDINANCE Amending Torrance Municipal Code Regarding
  Mitigation of Project-Related Adverse Impacts, and Determine that the Project is
  Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Pursuant to CEQA
  Guidelines Sections 15378 and 15061(b)(3). Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Finance Director that City Council:
  1) Conduct a public hearing on an amendment to the Torrance Municipal Code (TMC)
  Section 95.1.6(c) pertaining to the inclusion of provisions regarding the mitigation of
  project-related adverse impacts through the use of a Community Facilities District, as
  provided by the Mello-Roos Community Facilities Act of 1982; and
  2) Adopt a RESOLUTION adopting a Statement of Goals and Policies for the use of the
  Mello-Roos Community Facilities Act of 1982; and
  3) Adopt an ORDINANCE amending the TMC Section 95.1.6 of Chapter 5 of Article 1 of
  Division 9 entitled “Final Determination and Findings”; and
  4) Determine that the project is exempt from California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to Sections 15378 and 15061 (b)(3); and
  5) Approve an Ordinance Summary for publication.
  10B - STAFF REPORT
  10B - MATERIAL AVAILABLE

  10C. City Manager and Finance – Conduct Public Hearing and Adopt RESOLUTION
  Authorizing User & Regulatory Fees. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager and Finance Director that City Council:
  1) Conduct a public hearing on modified user and regulatory fees; and
  2) Adopt a RESOLUTION authorizing various user and regulatory fees and authorizing
  annual inflationary adjustments indexed to the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage
  Earners & Clerical Workers (CPI-W) May to May.
  10C - STAFF REPORT
  10C - PRESENTATION
  10C - MATERIAL AVAILABLE
  10C - SUPPLEMENTAL

11.  AGENCY AGENDAS – None Scheduled.

12.  2ND READING ORDINANCES – None Scheduled.

13.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS #2 (Limited up to a 15-minute period) Council Order –
  Sheikh, Gerson, Kaji, Kalani, Lewis, Mattucci, Mayor Chen This portion of the meeting
  is reserved for comments on items not on the agenda. Under the Ralph M. Brown Act,
  City Council cannot act on items raised during public comment, but may respond
  briefly to statements made or questions posed; request clarification; or refer the item
  to staff. Speakers under Orals are limited to either Oral Communications #1 or Oral
  Communications #2 and no longer than 1 minute per speaker. Time starts when you
  step up to the microphone. If presenting handout material to Council, please provide
  11 copies to the City Clerk before speaking. Handouts will be distributed while you
  speak.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

RECONVENE FROM CLOSED SESSION

15.  ADJOURNMENT
 15A. Adjournment of City Council meeting to Tuesday, September 17, 2024, at 5:00
  p.m. for closed session in the LeRoy J. Jackson Council Chamber.
15A - STAFF REPORT
